answer: Drawing graders at random, the system checks if their judgments match later audits. Each misaligned grader’s payment triggers a penalty, forcing targets to compute new signal-proofs per audit. Fake identities must wander the gale-locked proof bounds separately—no batching. Proofs are horizon-tied, so failed checks burn extra compute. Each reused signal requires recomputation. Cost: O(1) per Sybil, as proof costs can’t be parallelized.
